fieldNotes.title: Field Notes: 47-tile dashboard, founder couldn't answer 'are we growing?'
fieldNotes.source: Anonymous Head of Growth at a Bengaluru D2C food brand
fieldNotes.story:
Our Looker dashboard had 47 tiles by Q3. Reach, impressions, sentiment, EngagementRate v3, Composite Funnel Score, regional weekly cohort retention by acquisition channel. Bought a custom dashboard developer for ₹8 lakh to build it.

Founder asked at the all-hands: 'in one number, are we growing?' I opened the dashboard. Pointed to 4 different tiles. Couldn't give one number.

We scrapped the 47-tile dashboard. Replaced with 3 tiles: paid CAC (north star), D7 retention (gating metric), ROAS (kill criterion). Founder gets the answer in 4 seconds. **Decisions sped up enormously.** The 47 'rich' tiles? Most were vanity. The 3 we kept were the only ones that ever drove decisions.
fieldNotes.takeaway: A 47-tile dashboard hides decision-making behind data theatre. 3 tiles is the cap; everything else is decoration.

bossBattle.title: Boss Battle: the dashboard reset
bossBattle.setup: Sneha's inherited a marketing dashboard with 47 tiles, ~3 years of accumulated additions. CMO wants 'more visibility'. Sneha has 30 minutes to scope what to do.

stages.prompt: CMO says 'add 5 more tiles for sentiment, NPS, brand-recall, share-of-voice, AI-content-quality-score.' What's Sneha's response?

options.label: Counter: instead of adding, take the 47 + 5 = 52 down to 3. Identify the 3 metrics that drive decisions THIS quarter.
options.explain: Right. The dashboard delusion is solved by subtraction, not addition.

options.label: Add the 5 tiles.
options.explain: Repeats the trap. CMO will ask for 5 more next quarter.

options.label: Build a separate 'executive' dashboard with the 5 new ones.
options.explain: Now you have 47 + 5 + 1 'executive' dashboard. Trap deepens.

options.label: Paid CAC (north star) · D7 retention (gating) · ROAS (kill criterion).
options.explain: Three different roles, one number each. Founder/CMO/Sneha can all read it the same way.

options.label: Reach · Impressions · Engagement Rate.
options.explain: Three vanity metrics. None drives a decision; all of these can be huge while CAC tanks.

options.label: Revenue · Sessions · Conversions.
options.explain: Better than vanity but redundant — sessions and conversions are upstream of revenue. Pick distinct dimensions.

options.label: Pick 7 'just to be safe.'
options.explain: 7 is past the readability cap. 3 is the discipline.

stages.prompt: CMO insists on keeping the 47 tiles 'for archival access'. What's the move?

options.label: Move them to an 'archive' tab; keep main dashboard at 3 tiles. Anyone can drill in if they need.
options.explain: Right compromise. Default view is 3; the 47 are still accessible if someone insists.

options.label: Delete the 47 outright.
options.explain: Politically destabilizing; CMO will reverse. Compromise on placement, not on the 3-tile default.

options.label: Surrender; keep all 47 visible.
options.explain: Surrenders the win. Keep the 3-tile default view non-negotiable.

outcomes.perfect: S-tier. Sneha lands a 3-tile dashboard. Founder gets answers in 4 seconds; decisions speed up. CMO eventually thanks her at Q3 review.
outcomes.good: Solid. Compromise at 5 tiles instead of 3; not perfect but a 90% reduction is real progress.
outcomes.learn: Re-read the dashboard-delusion section. Adding tiles always feels productive; subtracting is what actually moves decisions.
